# Requirements Document

## Introduction

This spec covers the **Wardley Map diagram module** — a diagram type whose coordinates are *authored* rather than computed, and whose file belongs to an ecosystem ADP did not invent. It defines how a Wardley map is created, stored as an OnlineWardleyMaps `.owm` document beside its `.adp` registration file, parsed and written back without disturbing what a human wrote, rendered against its two semantic axes, and edited through commands, the context service and the property grid.

`src/diagrams/wardley-map/` is scaffolded, is in the solution, and its `Diagram.Definitions` already publishes `new DiagramOrigin("wardley", "map")` with a title and a description — so the type is discovered by `DiagramDefinitionDiscovery` and already offered in the Add dialog. Everything behind that entry is missing: it declares no `Extension`, registers no `IDiagramDocumentFactory`, and ships no `client/register.ts`, so adding one today writes a lone `map.adp` and the workspace shows `DiagramPanel`'s placeholder rather than a canvas.

**Why this type.** [`mindmap-diagram`](../mindmap-diagram/requirements.md) proved the pluggable model with a type whose positions are *computed* by the module and never written to the file. A Wardley map is the mirror image: its coordinates are *authored*, they carry the meaning, and moving a component is a strategic claim rather than a cosmetic one. [`c4-diagrams`](../c4-diagrams/requirements.md) has since shipped the middle case — computed by default, authored where the user drags — so the axis this type sits at the far end of is now a real spectrum rather than a pair. Two places where another type's answer must not be mistaken for a core rule are called out explicitly: layout (Requirement 7) and viewport filtering (Requirement 10.5).

### What this refresh changed *(against the 2026-08-23 revision)*

The first revision of this document was written when the mindmap was the only shipped diagram type, and it reasoned about seams that were then hypothetical. Most of them now exist and are used by two shipped modules. This revision holds the document to what the repository actually contains:

* **The one core change this spec anticipated is withdrawn.** The previous Requirement 8.4 asked core for a canvas background layer "beneath the elements and fixed to the coordinate space". No such seam is needed: a module claims a MIME type through `DiagramCanvasRegistration` and supplies a whole React component, which owns its own `<svg>`, its own `viewBox` and its own pan/zoom — as `C4Canvas` and `MindmapCanvas` both do. Axes and evolution bands are elements the module draws first in its own surface. **This spec now changes nothing in core.**
* **Four seams that did not exist are now required rather than invented**: `IDiagramSession`/`IDiagramSessionFactory` (Requirement 10.8), `IDiagramValidator` and `DiagramProblem` (Requirement 14), `IDiagramToolboxProvider` and `ToolboxItemDefinition` (Requirement 13), and `IContextPropertyProvider` with `ContextPropertyDefinition` (Requirement 15). The last three close what `tech.md`'s *Specifying a diagram type* names as a floor and this document previously left out.
* **The identity-sidecar citation was wrong and is corrected.** Requirement 4.2 previously claimed to reuse "the same mechanism `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 3.5 uses". That requirement does the opposite: it puts ADP's own data in the `.adp` file after the MIME line and states that a mindmap "stays **two** files, never three", and its Requirement 3.6 exists precisely to record that an earlier draft had assumed a sidecar. The real precedent is `c4-diagrams` Requirements 3.5–3.6, implemented as `C4LayoutSidecar` (`.layout.json`). Requirement 4 now cites that, and says why this type follows C4 rather than the mindmap.
* **`.wm` support was overstated** and is now bounded by what `DiagramDefinition.Extension` — a single string — can express (Requirement 2.6).
* **Requirement numbers 1–12 are unchanged in meaning**, because three other specs cite them by number: `c4-diagrams` Requirement 3.1 and `plantuml-uml` Requirement 6.1 both cite *Requirement 3* for the round-trip guarantee, and `azure-pipeline-diagram` Requirement 11.8 cites *Requirement 10.5* for answering a viewport with the whole document. New material is appended as Requirements 13–15 rather than folded in, so those citations stay true.

**Dependencies.** This spec redefines none of them:

* [`adp-diagram-ide`](../adp-diagram-ide/requirements.md) — the workspace shell, the pannable/zoomable canvas, read-only mode, the file-access layer.
* [`grpc-core-communication-specification`](../grpc-core-communication-specification/requirements.md) — `Element`, `Delta` (`add`/`remove`/`group`/`ungroup`), `Point2D`, and the `Any` payload extension point.
* [`add-diagram-action`](../add-diagram-action/requirements.md) and [`create-diagram-file`](../create-diagram-file/requirements.md) — the Add action, the `.adp` file and its MIME first line, the name field.
* [`mindmap-diagram`](../mindmap-diagram/requirements.md) — which introduced, and this spec reuses unchanged: `DiagramDefinition.Extension`, `IDiagramDocumentFactory`, `ContextSource.element_id`, `ContextScope.DIAGRAM_ELEMENT`, the `IDiagramSession` seam of its Requirement 13, and `DiagramService`'s `Open` + `UpdateView` legs.
* [`c4-diagrams`](../c4-diagrams/requirements.md) — the sidecar rule for data a foreign format has no place for (Requirements 3.5–3.6), the `body:` registration header, and the pure-function validator shape.
* [`context-service`](../context-service/requirements.md) — the selection chain and the pushing of a selection's actions.
* [`errors-and-warnings-panel`](../errors-and-warnings-panel/requirements.md) — where a validator's problems go (its Requirement 3).
* [`property-grid`](../property-grid/requirements.md) — the per-scope property provider, the read-only reason, the commit cadence.
* [`diagram-undo-redo`](../diagram-undo-redo/requirements.md) and `tech.md`'s **Commands** rule.

**Deliberately out of scope.** Editing the `.owm` as text with a live preview — the way onlinewardleymaps.com, the VS Code extension and the Obsidian plugin all work. It is a reasonable thing for ADP to want, it is a substantial feature in its own right, and nothing here precludes it: Requirement 3's round-trip is what a text editor would need anyway. Stated so its absence is a decision rather than an oversight.

## Alignment with Product Vision

* [product.md](../../steering/product.md)'s **"Don't reinvent, integrate"** — `.owm` is the de-facto maps-as-code format, shared by onlinewardleymaps.com, the VS Code extension, the Obsidian plugin and `cli-owm`. ADP reads and writes what that ecosystem already reads and writes, rather than a format of its own.
* product.md's **"Files are the source of truth"** — a map is two plain text files in the project folder, and a map ADP did not change is byte-identical after a save.
* product.md's **"Linkage over illustration"** — `submap` and `url` tie a map to other maps and to external material; Requirement 6.6 keeps those live rather than decorative.
* [tech.md](../../steering/tech.md)'s **Specifying a diagram type** — its four aspects are Requirements 2 and 3 (file format), Requirements 7 and 8 (visualization), Requirement 13 (toolbox) and Requirements 9 and 11 (context actions and commands).
* tech.md's **Commands** — every edit, including a drag, is a command with an inverse.
* tech.md's **Context** — a component becomes selectable by registering a resolver, exactly as a mindmap node and a C4 element did.
* tech.md's **Implementation order** — the requirement order below follows model, persistence, wire, UI, logic, so the tasks can too.
* [structure.md](../../steering/structure.md)'s **dependency direction** — the module depends on core; core never depends on the module.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — A Wardley map is created through the Add action

**User Story:** As an architect, I want to create a Wardley map from the Add dialog like any other diagram, so that starting one costs nothing new to learn.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the user opens the Add dialog THEN **Wardley Map** SHALL appear under the `wardley` vendor group by the `Title` its existing `Diagram.Definitions` entry already carries, through discovery alone.
2. WHEN the user selects it and has not edited the name THEN the suggested file name SHALL be `map`, made collision-free per `create-diagram-file` Requirement 2.2 (`map-2`, `map-3`, …) — derived from the origin's `Type` segment, with no per-type special case.
3. WHEN the user confirms THEN the system SHALL create both `<name>.adp`, whose first line is `wardley/map`, and `<name>.owm`, through the shared create-file command and the module's `IDiagramDocumentFactory`, with no change to the Add flow.
4. WHEN the empty `.owm` body is written THEN it SHALL be a valid, minimal document — a `title` line carrying the file's base name — which opens as an empty map showing its axes and nothing else. A map with no components SHALL be a valid map, not an error.
5. IF writing either file fails THEN neither SHALL be left behind, per `create-diagram-file` Requirement 5.
6. WHEN the module registers its document factory THEN it SHALL be the single registration `IDiagramDocumentFactory` describes, resolved by origin. A definition declaring an extension without one is a deployment error `DiagramDocumentFactories.Verify` reports at startup, so this registration is not optional once Requirement 2.2 is met.

### Requirement 2 — Registration in `.adp`, body in the `.owm` sibling

**User Story:** As an architect, I want my map to live in a real `.owm` file, so that I can open it in onlinewardleymaps.com, VS Code or Obsidian without converting anything.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a Wardley map exists on disk THEN it SHALL be `<name>.adp` (first line `wardley/map`) plus `<name>.owm` holding the OnlineWardleyMaps DSL, sharing one base name in one folder.
2. WHEN the module declares itself THEN it SHALL set `DiagramDefinition.Extension` to `".owm"` — the member `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 2.2 added, which core uses to name the sibling by construction rather than carrying a MIME-to-extension map. No new core mechanism SHALL be introduced for this.
3. WHEN an `.adp` file naming `wardley/map` is opened THEN `DiagramFileRouter` SHALL route it by its MIME first line and `DiagramFilePair` SHALL name its `.owm` sibling; a save SHALL write that sibling, and the `.adp` file SHALL NOT be rewritten by any edit.
4. IF the `.owm` sibling is missing THEN the map SHALL open as an empty map (Requirement 1.4) and the sibling SHALL be created on the first save, rather than failing to open.
5. WHEN an `.owm` file is present without an `.adp` sibling — a map authored elsewhere and dropped into the project — THEN it SHALL still be openable through the router's bare-body path, and the `.adp` file SHALL NOT be created implicitly. This works because `.owm` is a **distinctive** extension in `azure-pipeline-diagram` Requirement 2.2's sense: one vendor owns it outright, so `DiagramFileRouter.AmbiguousExtensions()` never reports it and no user choice is needed.
6. WHERE a map arrives as `.wm` — an extension the ecosystem's own tooling also accepts for this DSL — THEN the module SHALL parse it identically, and it SHALL be openable by giving it an `.adp` registration carrying a `body:` header naming the file, the mechanism `c4-diagrams` Requirement 2.4 introduced and `DiagramFilePair.BodyOf` implements. A bare `.wm` with no registration SHALL NOT be routed, because `DiagramDefinition.Extension` is one string and this module SHALL NOT be the reason it becomes a list — `azure-pipeline-diagram` Requirement 2.1 already owns widening it, and this type SHALL reuse that when it lands rather than duplicating it. The **created** extension SHALL always be `.owm`.

### Requirement 3 — Reading and writing `.owm` without disturbing it

**User Story:** As a map author, I want ADP to leave alone every part of my file it did not change, so that opening a map in ADP never shows up as a diff I have to review.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a map ADP has not changed is saved THEN the resulting file SHALL be **byte-identical** to what was read — statement order, blank lines, comments, indentation, line endings and trailing newline included.
2. WHEN ADP changes one thing THEN it SHALL rewrite **only the statements that thing occupies**, leaving every other line exactly as the author wrote it. This requires a **concrete syntax tree** — every statement holding the span it came from — rather than a model the writer regenerates, because a regenerator reformats a hand-authored document on the first save. `azure-pipeline-diagram`'s design records this as "the same decision `wardley-map` made and `C4Document` implements"; the shape is settled and this module SHALL follow it rather than re-derive it.
3. WHEN a statement is encountered that this module does not recognise — a keyword from a newer DSL version, or one this spec does not cover — THEN it SHALL be preserved verbatim through a round trip and SHALL NOT be dropped, reordered or reported as an error. Forward compatibility is a property of the writer, not a promise to keep chasing the DSL.
4. IF a file cannot be parsed at all THEN the map SHALL open in the unavailable state carrying the parser's message and, where it has one, the line number — and the file SHALL NOT be rewritten while it is unparseable, so a broken file is never made worse (`c4-diagrams` Requirement 3.4).
5. WHEN a line is syntactically valid but semantically broken — a link naming a component that does not exist, a coordinate outside `0..1` — THEN the map SHALL still open, the problem SHALL be reported through Requirement 14, and the rest of the map SHALL render. A map is a thinking tool; refusing to show it because one link is dangling is worse than showing it with the link marked.
6. WHEN the module writes a file THEN it SHALL do so through the backend's existing file-access layer and atomically (temporary file in the same folder, then move into place), to the standard `create-diagram-file` Requirement 3.3 sets.
7. WHERE ADP holds data the DSL has no place for — element identities (Requirement 4) — it SHALL go in a sidecar file ADP owns, never as a comment or a smuggled annotation inside the `.owm`, per tech.md's *Specifying a diagram type* and `c4-diagrams` Requirement 3.5.

### Requirement 4 — Every element has a stable identity, and the file does not provide one

**User Story:** As an architect, I want my selection, my undo history and my links to survive renaming a component, so that renaming is an edit rather than a small catastrophe.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module needs to identify an element THEN it SHALL use an ADP-assigned `ShortGuid`, not the component's name. The `.owm` format has **no identifier of any kind**: components are named, and `evolve`, links and pipelines all reference them by name. Name-as-identity would make every rename a delete-plus-add, breaking the current selection, every undo entry that mentions the element, and the pushed element ids on the delta stream.
2. WHEN identities are stored THEN they SHALL live in a **sidecar file beside the `.owm`**, following `c4-diagrams` Requirements 3.5–3.6 and the `C4LayoutSidecar` (`.layout.json`) it produced, so the `.owm` stays a standard document ADP has not annotated.
   * This is **deliberately not** the mechanism `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 3.5 chose. That requirement puts ADP's own data in the `.adp` file after the MIME line and states a mindmap "stays **two** files, never three" — and its Requirement 3.6 records that an earlier draft had assumed a sidecar and was wrong to. The two types differ in the fact that decides it: a `.mm` node carries a native `ID` attribute, so the mindmap has identities to *use* and only a little else to store, while an `.owm` component has none at all and this module must store an identity for **every element on the map**. That is a growing, per-element structure, which is what the sidecar rule exists for.
3. WHEN a map is opened whose elements have no recorded identity — authored elsewhere, or the sidecar is missing — THEN the system SHALL assign identities on load and persist them on the first save, and the map SHALL be fully usable in the meantime. A map opened and not edited SHALL produce no write at all, as `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 3.4 requires of assigned ids.
4. WHEN a component is renamed THEN its identity SHALL be unchanged, and every statement referring to it by name — links, `evolve`, pipeline membership — SHALL be rewritten in the same command, so the file stays internally consistent.
5. IF the sidecar is lost, unreadable, or inconsistent with the `.owm` (an id naming a component that no longer exists) THEN the system SHALL re-derive what it can by name, discard what it cannot, and continue. The sidecar SHALL be an **optimisation, never a dependency** (`c4-diagrams` Requirement 3.6) — the `.owm` is the document, and a cosmetic file's corruption SHALL never be the reason a map fails to open.
6. WHEN two components share a name — which the DSL permits and which makes references ambiguous — THEN it SHALL be reported through Requirement 14 and both elements SHALL stay distinguishable by identity.

### Requirement 5 — The map model: components, links and pipelines

**User Story:** As an architect, I want the things I drew to come back as the things I drew, so that a round trip through ADP is lossless.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a `component`, `anchor`, `market`, `ecosystem` or `submap` statement is read THEN the system SHALL produce a positioned element carrying its name, its kind and its coordinates.
2. WHEN a coordinate pair `[a, b]` is read THEN the system SHALL interpret **`a` as visibility (the value-chain axis) and `b` as maturity (the evolution axis)**, both in `0..1`. This is the reverse of `Point2D(x, y)`, and the conversion SHALL live in exactly one place so no other code has to remember it.
3. WHEN a link `A->B`, a flow link `A+>B`, or a link with context `A->B; text` is read THEN the system SHALL produce an element naming both endpoints by identity, carrying the link's kind and its context text.
4. WHEN a `pipeline` is read THEN the system SHALL produce a container holding its child components, where a child carries only an evolution position and takes its visibility from the parent — the current nested form `pipeline Parent{ … }`. The **legacy** two-coordinate form SHALL be readable, and SHALL be written back in whichever form it was read (Requirement 3.2).
5. WHEN an element carries a `label [dx, dy]` offset THEN the system SHALL preserve it through a round trip and SHALL honour it when rendering. The offset is in pixels rather than map coordinates — a property of the format, which ADP reproduces rather than corrects.
6. WHEN map-level statements are read — `title`, `size [w, h]`, `style` — THEN they SHALL be preserved and applied where they affect rendering. They are properties of the map, not elements on it.
7. WHEN the model is tested THEN parsing and writing SHALL be exercisable from a plain string with no file, no canvas and no connection, per the *Dependency Management* rule below.

### Requirement 6 — The strategy vocabulary

**User Story:** As an architect, I want the annotations that make a map a strategy tool rather than a picture, so that what I record about movement and intent survives.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an `evolve` statement is read THEN the component SHALL be shown at **both** its current and its target maturity, joined by a movement indicator, since the pair is the point of the statement. `evolve Name->NewName x` SHALL additionally carry the name the component takes when it arrives.
2. WHEN `inertia` is present on a component THEN it SHALL be preserved and indicated on the map.
3. WHEN a `(build)`, `(buy)` or `(outsource)` decorator is present THEN it SHALL be preserved and indicated.
4. WHEN `pioneers`, `settlers` or `townplanners` areas are declared THEN they SHALL be preserved and rendered as areas behind the elements they cover.
5. WHEN an `accelerator` or `deaccelerator` is declared THEN it SHALL be preserved and rendered at its position.
6. WHEN a `submap` or a `url` is read THEN it SHALL be preserved, and activating a `submap` SHALL open the map it names through the same navigation path any other diagram is opened by — not through a Wardley-specific mechanism.
7. WHEN a `note` is read THEN it SHALL be preserved and rendered as free text at its position.
8. WHEN an `annotation` is read THEN it SHALL be preserved with **all** of its coordinates: the DSL permits one numbered annotation pinned at several places, which a one-element-one-position model does not express directly. How that is represented is a design decision; that none of the positions may be lost is not.
9. WHEN a component carries any of the decorations in 6.2–6.3 THEN they SHALL be legible **on the canvas** without entering an edit mode or opening a panel — preserving them through a round trip is Requirement 3's job, and showing them is this one's. The same values SHALL also appear in the property grid (Requirement 15), which is where their exact form is read rather than merely noticed.

### Requirement 7 — Coordinates are authored, and moving something is an edit

**User Story:** As an architect, I want dragging a component to change my map, so that I can think by moving things rather than by editing numbers.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module positions an element THEN the position SHALL come **from the document**. This module SHALL NOT compute a layout, and SHALL NOT contain one.
2. WHEN the user drags an element on the canvas THEN the system SHALL treat it as a **document edit**: a command whose inverse restores the previous coordinates, written back to the `.owm`, pushed to every other client, and recorded on the project's history. Position is meaning here — moving a component right asserts that it is more evolved — so a drag is never a view-only change.
3. WHEN an element is dragged THEN its coordinates SHALL be clamped to `0..1` on both axes; a component cannot be more evolved than commodity.
4. WHEN a component inside a pipeline is dragged THEN only its evolution position SHALL change, since its visibility is the parent's (Requirement 5.4).
5. WHEN the map is open in read-only mode THEN dragging SHALL be rejected like any other document edit, and SHALL not be offered.
6. WHEN this requirement is read against `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 5 and `c4-diagrams` Requirement 8 THEN the three answers are deliberately different and core SHALL be able to serve all of them without knowing which it is serving: the mindmap computes positions and never writes them; C4 computes them and writes the ones the user overrode into a sidecar; this type reads them from the document and writes them back into it. **Anything in core that has to ask which is a defect in core.**

### Requirement 8 — Rendering the map

**User Story:** As an architect, I want to see the axes, the evolution bands and my components in the places I put them, so that the picture means what a Wardley map means.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a map is opened THEN the system SHALL render a bounded `0..1` × `0..1` coordinate space, with the value-chain axis vertical (the user need at the top, invisible components at the bottom) and the evolution axis horizontal (genesis at the left, commodity at the right).
2. WHEN the evolution axis is drawn THEN it SHALL show the four stages with boundaries at **0.175**, **0.400** and **0.700**, labelled **Genesis**, **Custom Built**, **Product `(+rental)`** and **Commodity `(+utility)`**. These constants are not published in the DSL documentation; they are derived from the reference renderer's own `EvoOffsets` (`custom: 3.5`, `product: 8`, `commodity: 14`, each divided by 20) and SHALL be pinned in the module with a test and a comment citing that source, so nobody re-derives them from a search result.
3. WHEN an element is rendered THEN its kind SHALL be visually distinguishable — an anchor from a component from a market from a submap — and the annotations of Requirement 6 SHALL be visible on it per Requirement 6.9.
4. WHEN the axes, bands and their labels are drawn THEN they SHALL be drawn **by the module**, and **no core change SHALL be required to allow it**. A module claims its MIME types through `DiagramCanvasRegistration` in its own `client/register.ts` and supplies a component that owns its entire `<svg>` surface — its `viewBox`, its pan and zoom, its layer order — exactly as `C4Canvas` and `MindmapCanvas` do. The axis chrome is therefore simply what this module draws first, beneath its elements. *(The previous revision of this requirement asked core for a background-layer seam; the registration shape that shipped since makes one unnecessary, and asking for it now would be a core change with nothing behind it.)*
5. WHEN the canvas is panned or zoomed THEN the axis chrome SHALL scale with the map rather than float over it, since a component's position is only meaningful against its own axes. Stage **labels** MAY hold a readable size, per Requirement 8.2's legibility rule; the boundaries they name SHALL NOT.
6. WHEN a problem was reported against an element (Requirement 14) THEN that element SHALL be marked on the canvas, so a dangling link is visible where it is rather than only in a list.
7. WHEN the module ships its client code THEN it SHALL be `diagrams/wardley-map/client/` with a `register.ts` exporting its registrations, discovered by the shell's `import.meta.glob` scan with no edit to the shell — the client's counterpart to the backend's assembly scan.

### Requirement 9 — Every change is a command

**User Story:** As a developer of EtAlii.Adp, I want every map edit to be an `ICommand` with an inverse, so that undo, validation and multi-client delivery come from the system rather than from this module.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN anything changes a map's document state THEN it SHALL be an `ICommand` with a matching `ICommandHandler<TCommand>` dispatched through `IHistoryStack`, per `tech.md`'s Commands rule; nothing SHALL edit the `.owm` inline.
2. WHEN a handler succeeds THEN it SHALL report the command that reverses it as `CommandResult.Inverse`, so the change becomes undoable on the project's history without this module implementing undo.
3. WHEN the module defines its commands THEN they SHALL cover at least: add an element, remove an element, move an element, rename an element, set or clear a link, set or clear `evolve`, set or clear `inertia` and the build/buy/outsource decorators, and add or remove a component from a pipeline.
4. WHEN a command is rejected — the element is gone, the name is already taken, the map is read-only — THEN the handler SHALL return a `CommandResult` carrying a message for the user, not throw.
5. WHEN a handler runs THEN it SHALL validate its own preconditions against current state, since undo and redo dispatch it again later.
6. WHEN a rename is undone THEN every statement rewritten under Requirement 4.4 SHALL be restored with it, so an undo leaves the file exactly as it was rather than partially renamed.
7. WHEN handlers are placed THEN they SHALL live in a `Commands` subfolder of the module and be registered through the module's own `AddWardleyMapCommands` extension, as the mindmap and C4 modules' are.
8. WHEN the same edit is reachable from the canvas, the context menu, the keyboard and the property grid THEN all four SHALL dispatch the **same** command, so there is one implementation, one inverse and one validation path behind every route to it.

### Requirement 10 — The core delta and viewport contract

**User Story:** As a developer of EtAlii.Adp, I want a Wardley map expressed entirely in the existing element and delta vocabulary, so that this module tests the contract rather than extending it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a client opens a map THEN it SHALL do so over `DiagramService.Open` with the `.adp` file's project-relative path, and report its viewport through the unary `UpdateView` — the two correlated legs `tech.md`'s *gRPC call shapes* requires. The client SHALL NOT name the `.owm` sibling.
2. WHEN an element is sent THEN it SHALL be one core `Element`: `id` the identity of Requirement 4, `position` converted from the document's `[visibility, maturity]`, `type` a mime-style string under `wardley/map` naming the element kind, and `payload` a module-owned message defined in `diagrams/wardley-map/api/` and packed into the core `Any`, without modifying the core contract files.
3. WHEN elements appear, change or disappear THEN the system SHALL express it with the existing `Add` and `Remove` actions, an edit being an `Add` carrying the element in its new state. No new `Delta` action SHALL be added for this module.
4. WHEN a pipeline is sent THEN it SHALL use the existing `Group` and `Ungroup` actions, the parent as the group element and its children as the sources — the second independent use of those two actions after mindmap folding.
5. WHEN a viewport is reported THEN the module MAY answer with the entire map. A Wardley map is a bounded space holding tens of elements, so viewport filtering has nothing to do here; `adp-diagram-ide` Requirement 4.3's virtualization is a capability core offers, not an obligation every module owes. No filter SHALL be implemented merely to satisfy a rule.
6. WHEN a connection reconnects, or several clients edit the same map THEN re-baselining and reconciliation SHALL be the core behaviour, with no module-specific mechanism.
7. WHEN the `.owm` or its sidecar changes on disk outside ADP THEN the system SHALL reload and push the difference as deltas, and that reload SHALL NOT be undoable.
8. WHEN the module serves an open map THEN it SHALL do so by registering an `IDiagramSessionFactory` returning an `IDiagramSession` — the fourth registration seam `mindmap-diagram` Requirement 13 established and `IDiagramSession` now defines. Core owns the stream, the authorization and the connection lifetime; this module owns `Baseline()`, `UpdateView(viewport)` and the `Changed` event that carries an edit from any connection into this one's view. The factory SHALL be given the `.owm` path as its body and MAY ignore the `registrationPath` it is handed, since a `wardley/map` registration carries nothing beyond its MIME line.

### Requirement 11 — Selection, focus and actions

**User Story:** As an architect, I want the component I click to become the selection everywhere in the IDE, so that the property grid and the ribbon follow what I am looking at.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the user selects an element on the canvas THEN the client SHALL report it through `ContextService.Select` as a nested selection: the `.adp` file as the outer level, the element as its `child` with source `DIAGRAM_CANVAS` and its `element_id`. Both the `ContextSource.element_id` member and the `DIAGRAM_ELEMENT` scope already exist; this module SHALL reuse them and SHALL NOT add a variant.
2. WHEN an element is made selectable THEN it SHALL be by registering an `IContextSourceResolver` for this module, with no change inside the context service.
3. WHEN an element selection is pushed THEN it SHALL carry backend-resolved detail — the element's name, its kind, its coordinates and its evolution stage — so a consumer can show what is selected without a lookup of its own. What the **property grid** shows is Requirement 15, which owns the full list; this criterion owns only that the pushed selection is self-describing.
4. WHEN an element is selected THEN its actions SHALL be pushed alongside it, contributed through an `IContextActionProvider` for the diagram-element scope, and SHALL reach the ribbon, the right-click menu and the keyboard through the one path every other action uses.
5. WHEN actions are offered THEN they SHALL cover the edits of Requirement 9.3, and each SHALL be described by the backend as data, including any shortcut. The client SHALL hold no key-to-action table.
6. WHEN an action does not apply — an unlink on an element with no link, any edit in read-only mode — THEN it SHALL NOT be offered, so the menu agrees with what would succeed.
7. WHEN the selection changes from elsewhere THEN the canvas SHALL bring the selected element into view and SHALL NOT re-react to a selection it produced itself.
8. Multi-selection is out of scope, per `context-service` Requirement 2.8.

### Requirement 12 — Pluggable registration as a diagram type

**User Story:** As a developer of EtAlii.Adp, I want this module to plug in exactly where the two before it did, so that a third diagram type demonstrates a repeatable path rather than a third special case.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the backend starts THEN the module SHALL be discovered through the existing `Diagram.Definitions` reflection scan, as it already is, with `Extension` the only addition to what it publishes.
2. WHEN the module organises its code THEN it SHALL be `diagrams/wardley-map/` with `backend/` (`EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.WardleyMap` and its `.Tests`), `api/` and `client/`, per `structure.md` — the layout the mindmap and C4 modules already follow, and which this module's scaffolding already has.
3. WHEN the module registers itself THEN each of its seams SHALL be **one registration through an existing extension point**, gathered into one `AddWardleyMap` extension method per tech.md's registration rule. The seams are: `IDiagramDocumentFactory` (Requirement 1.6), `IDiagramSessionFactory` (Requirement 10.8), `IContextSourceResolver` (Requirement 11.2), `IContextActionProvider` (Requirement 11.4), `IDiagramToolboxProvider` (Requirement 13), `IDiagramValidator` (Requirement 14), `IContextPropertyProvider` (Requirement 15), and the client's `register.ts` (Requirement 8.7). Every one of them exists today and is used by at least one shipped module.
4. IF core canvas, storage, sync, context or command code is inspected THEN it SHALL contain no Wardley-specific type check, import or branch. **This spec anticipates no core change at all** — the one its previous revision named has been withdrawn (see the Introduction), and nothing has replaced it.
5. WHEN this module is complete THEN the three shipped notations SHALL differ in **who owns position** — computed and never written (mindmap), computed with authored overrides in a sidecar (C4), authored in the document and written back (this type) — and core SHALL be unchanged by that difference. **This is the acceptance test for the pluggable diagram-type model**, and a core change discovered to be necessary is a finding to report, not a step to take quietly.
6. WHEN the module reaches each state THEN `docs/diagrams.md`'s `wardley/map` row SHALL be updated per CLAUDE.md — to **📝 Specified** while this document exists, which is the state the catalog's own legend defines and which the row is corrected to as part of this refresh, then 🛠️ work-in-progress and ✅ implemented as the work proceeds. Its Notes column SHALL gain the `.owm` DSL reference, as the mindmap row cites `.mm`.

### Requirement 13 — Toolbox

**User Story:** As an architect starting a map, I want the things a Wardley map is made of offered to me, so that I do not have to remember the DSL's vocabulary to put something on the canvas.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module contributes toolbox entries THEN it SHALL do so by registering one `IDiagramToolboxProvider` keyed by its origin, whose `Items` are `ToolboxItemDefinition`s — described as data the client renders without understanding, exactly as context actions are.
2. WHEN the palette is shown THEN it SHALL offer at least: **Component**, **Anchor** (the user need), **Market**, **Ecosystem**, **Submap**, **Pipeline**, **Note** and **Annotation** — the element kinds Requirements 5 and 6 model and a user creates rather than derives.
3. WHEN an entry is dropped THEN its `DropActionId` SHALL name a context action this module already contributes under Requirement 11.4, so the drop, the menu item and the keyboard shortcut are one implementation with one command and one inverse behind them.
4. WHEN a **component-shaped** entry is dropped on empty canvas THEN the element SHALL be created at the dropped position, which is the map's meaning for it — this is the one type where a drop position is a claim rather than a convenience, and it SHALL NOT be discarded in favour of a computed one.
5. WHEN an entry is dropped in read-only mode THEN it SHALL be refused with the reason every other refused edit gives, and the palette SHALL show its entries as unavailable rather than hiding them.
6. WHERE an element kind cannot sensibly be created by dropping — a **link**, which needs two endpoints — THEN it SHALL NOT be a toolbox entry, and it SHALL be created through the context action of Requirement 9.3 instead. tech.md requires a type whose elements cannot be created that way to say so and say how they are created; this criterion is that statement.
7. WHEN the Toolbox panel host does not yet exist THEN this requirement SHALL still be implementable and testable — a provider's `Items` are static per type and assertable without a UI, which is why tech.md asks a type to state its toolbox even while the panel that shows it arrives separately.

### Requirement 14 — Telling the user what is wrong with their map

**User Story:** As an architect, I want to be told when my map says something impossible, so that a dangling link or an out-of-range coordinate is visible rather than silently rendered.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the module contributes rules THEN it SHALL do so by registering one `IDiagramValidator` keyed by its origin, so its problems reach the Errors & Warnings panel exactly as any other type's do (`errors-and-warnings-panel` Requirement 3.1). Core SHALL NOT interpret, rank or rewrite what it returns.
2. WHEN a link, an `evolve`, or a pipeline membership names a component that does not exist THEN it SHALL be reported as an **error**, naming both the missing name and the statement that referenced it.
3. WHEN a coordinate falls outside `0..1` on either axis THEN it SHALL be reported as an **error**: the map's space is bounded, and a component outside it cannot be drawn where the file says it is.
4. WHEN two components share a name THEN it SHALL be reported as an **error** (Requirement 4.6), because every reference to that name in the file is ambiguous.
5. WHEN a map has no `anchor` THEN it SHOULD be reported as a **warning** — a value chain with no user need at the top is a map missing the thing it hangs from — and this SHALL NOT block the map from opening or being edited.
6. WHEN a `submap` names a map that is not in the project, or a `url` cannot be resolved, THEN it SHALL be reported as a **warning**, since the reference may be to something legitimately outside the workspace.
7. WHEN a problem is reported THEN it SHALL carry a **line location** where the rule judged the text and an **element location** where it judged the model, using `DiagramProblemLineLocation` and `DiagramProblemElementLocation`, so the panel can take the user to it and Requirement 8.6 can mark it on the canvas.
8. WHEN a problem's `RuleId` is set THEN it SHALL be prefixed with this module's short name — `wardley.link-target-missing`, `wardley.coordinate-out-of-range` — per `DiagramProblem`'s convention, so a problem in a log names the module that owns it.
9. WHEN validation runs THEN it SHALL be a **pure function from a parsed model to problems**, testable from a plain `.owm` string with no file, canvas or connection — the shape `c4-diagrams` established for `C4RuleSet` and `azure-pipeline-diagram` Requirement 10.9 restates. It SHALL be bounded in time, so a pathological document cannot hang a "Validate all" (`errors-and-warnings-panel` Requirement 3.5).

### Requirement 15 — What a Wardley element shows in the Property Grid

**User Story:** As an architect who has selected a component, I want the panel to tell me exactly where it sits and what I have claimed about it, so that I can read and correct the numbers rather than only drag them.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a Wardley element is selected THEN the module SHALL contribute its properties by registering an `IContextPropertyProvider` for `ContextScope.DiagramElement`, resolving the element from the `ContextTarget` it is given — already resolved and containment-checked by the service layer. Registering it SHALL be one line, and core SHALL learn nothing about Wardley maps.
2. WHEN a **component-shaped element** (component, anchor, market, ecosystem, submap) is selected THEN the panel SHALL show at least: its **name**, its **kind**, its **visibility** and **maturity** as numbers, the **evolution stage** those resolve to (Requirement 8.2), its `evolve` target and the name it takes on arrival where it has one, its `inertia`, its build/buy/outsource decorator, its `label` offset, and its `url` or `submap` target where present.
3. WHEN a **link** is selected THEN the panel SHALL show its two endpoints by name, its kind (plain or flow), and its context text where it has one.
4. WHEN a **pipeline** is selected THEN the panel SHALL show its name, its visibility, and its children with their evolution positions; and WHEN a pipeline **child** is selected THEN its visibility SHALL be shown as the parent's, with a reason saying so rather than as a value of its own (Requirement 5.4).
5. WHEN a property is contributed THEN `ReadOnlyReason` SHALL be **empty** — editable — for the name, the two coordinates, the `evolve` target, the `inertia`, the decorator and the link's context text; these are the author's own claims and the panel is a legitimate place to state them precisely. It SHALL be **non-empty** for the derived evolution stage, which is a reading of the maturity rather than a value in the file, and the reason SHALL say to change the maturity instead.
6. WHEN a property is **absent** from the document THEN it SHALL NOT be contributed at all, rather than contributed with an empty `Value` — the distinction `ContextPropertyDefinition` preserves deliberately, and which here separates "this component has no inertia" from "this component has an empty one".
7. WHEN an editable property is changed THEN `SetAsync` SHALL dispatch the **same `ICommand`** the canvas and the context menu use (Requirement 9.8), so typing `0.42` into the maturity row and dragging the component to the same place are one implementation and one undo entry. WHERE a value is rejected — a coordinate outside `0..1`, a name already taken — the result SHALL carry the reason for the panel to show, and the document SHALL be unchanged.
8. WHEN a value is committed THEN it SHALL follow the contract's cadence: **on Enter or blur, once per committed edit, never per keystroke** (`property-grid` Requirement 6). Each commit rewrites a statement in a file another ecosystem reads, and per-keystroke writes would put that file through a state per character typed.
9. WHEN properties are grouped THEN `Group` SHALL separate **identity** (name, kind), **position** (visibility, maturity, stage, label offset), **strategy** (`evolve`, `inertia`, decorator) and **links** (`url`, `submap`), because a component carries more than reads comfortably as one flat list.
10. WHERE the contract's editors are `Line`, `Text` and `Toggle` THEN every property above is served by them: coordinates and names by `Line`, a note's text by `Text`, and `inertia` by `Toggle`. **This type needs no new editor**, which is worth stating because `azure-pipeline-diagram` Requirement 13.14 does owe one — a `Choice` for its `dependsOn` — and this module SHALL NOT be the reason that lands earlier.
11. WHEN a map is open in read-only mode THEN every property SHALL be contributed with a `ReadOnlyReason` naming that mode rather than being withheld, so the panel still answers what the element is.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

* **Single Responsibility Principle**: the `.owm` parser/writer, the identity sidecar, the map model, the element/delta mapping, the session, the context resolver, the action provider, the toolbox provider, the validator, the property provider and the canvas rendering are separate, independently testable concerns.
* **Modular Design**: `EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.WardleyMap`, `diagrams/wardley-map/api` and `diagrams/wardley-map/client` depend only on core abstractions; nothing in core depends on the module, and core stays compilable with zero diagram modules present.
* **Dependency Management**: the parser/writer SHALL be usable without gRPC, without the filesystem and without a browser — given text, it returns a model, and given a model and the original text, it returns new text. The validator SHALL be a pure function over that model (Requirement 14.9).
* **Clear Interfaces**: the integration surface is the eight registrations Requirement 12.3 lists, and nothing else.
* **Code style**: backend code SHALL satisfy `src/.editorconfig` as `dotnet format style --verify-no-changes --severity info` checks it, per CLAUDE.md and `quality-gates` Requirement 5; client code SHALL follow the same file's TypeScript sections.

### Performance

* Opening a map SHALL be one file read plus one sidecar read, and SHALL be fast enough to feel immediate for the map sizes this notation is used at (tens of elements, occasionally low hundreds).
* An edit SHALL rewrite the statements it touches, not re-serialize the document, so save cost tracks the size of the change rather than the size of the map.
* Because the whole map is delivered (Requirement 10.5), the baseline `Add` SHALL be one message rather than a stream of per-element ones.
* Validation SHALL be linear in the document's length and bounded in time (Requirement 14.9).

### Security

* The module SHALL read and write only through the backend's file-access layer, within the opened workspace folder; an absolute path SHALL never reach a client.
* A `url`, a `submap` target, a component name or a note read from a file authored elsewhere is untrusted input: it SHALL be rendered as text, never interpreted as markup or script, and a `submap` or `url` SHALL only resolve within the authorized workspace or as an external link the user explicitly activates.
* A malformed `.owm` SHALL not be able to exhaust memory or time — parsing SHALL be linear in the file's length, with no construct that can expand.

### Reliability

* A save SHALL be atomic and SHALL never leave an `.owm` observable in a partial state; creation SHALL leave both files or neither.
* A map ADP did not change SHALL round-trip byte-identically (Requirement 3.1). This is the module's headline correctness property and SHALL be tested against a corpus of real maps, including ones using constructs this spec does not model.
* A lost or inconsistent identity sidecar SHALL degrade to re-derivation, never to a map that will not open (Requirement 4.5).
* A validator that throws or hangs SHALL cost its own diagram's results and nothing more (`errors-and-warnings-panel` Requirements 3.4–3.5).
* Every bug found while implementing or verifying this spec SHALL be covered by a test, or recorded in `tests.md`, per CLAUDE.md.

### Usability

* The four evolution stages SHALL be legible on the canvas at default zoom, since a component's position means nothing without them.
* A map authored in onlinewardleymaps.com, VS Code or Obsidian SHALL open in ADP looking recognisably like the same map, and SHALL open in those tools again afterwards.
* The user SHALL be able to tell an element they positioned from one ADP positioned, which — since ADP never positions anything here (Requirement 7.1) — means every element on the canvas is the author's own claim.
* A problem SHALL be reachable from where it is seen: marked on the canvas (Requirement 8.6), listed in the panel, and locatable in the text by line (Requirement 14.7).
